analysis.title: Core inflation reaccelerates, supporting a third Fed hike
key_insights: September CPI surprised to the upside: headline +0.65% m/m and 3.7% y/y, core +0.33% m/m and 2.6% y/y. Core was above the 0.2% consensus for a second consecutive month.
Energy drove the headline acceleration. Gasoline rose about 9.5% m/m on Middle East supply concerns, and energy contributed nearly 40bps of the 65bps monthly gain.
Core goods rose 0.25% m/m versus a 0.07% three-month average. Information technology pricing rose 91bps m/m on supply constraints and AI-related demand, and new and used vehicle prices moved higher.

Core services rose 0.37% m/m, up from 0.33% in August and well above the 0.20% three-month average. Hotels rose more than 2% m/m and added nearly 4bps to core. Airfare rose 1.2% m/m. Primary rent and owners-equivalent rent were a bit firmer than their three-month average.

UBS revised its Fed call to a third hike in March 2027, after hikes in September and December 2026, then on hold until late 2027 and a first cut in late 2027. Three hikes would fully reverse the 2025 insurance cuts.
An October hike is a close call after back-to-back upside inflation surprises. Vice Chair Jefferson and NY Fed President Williams have signaled a preference for more gradual tightening.
Growth supports the call: 1H growth near 2.5% annualized and 3Q tracking 3%. Core PCE remains near 3%, so the Fed can focus on inflation over labor market concerns.
The tightening rationale is risk management against three overlapping shocks: Middle East supply disruption, AI investment-cycle demand pressure, and trade policy uncertainty.
UBS's path is more dovish than market pricing. Markets discount about 3.8 additional hikes, nearly 5 in total including September, against UBS's three.

tension_points.bull_case: Stronger goods and services inflation, firm growth (1H near 2.5%, 3Q tracking 3%) and core PCE near 3% support a third hike in March 2027, with the Fed focused on inflation over labor market risk.
tension_points.bear_case: Tighter financial conditions or slower growth could reduce the need for additional tightening and weaken the case for a third hike.
tension_points.what_invalidates: Tighter financial conditions or slower growth that reduce the need for additional policy tightening.

theme_stances.key_argument: Simultaneous acceleration in core goods and core services keeps the Fed focused on inflation risks and reinforces higher-for-longer policy expectations.
theme_stances.evidence: revise our forecast to include a third rate hike in March 2027
